title: Heart-Health-Study
summary:
Cardiovascular diseases are still the leading cause of death in Germany—ranking even higher than cancer. Furthermore, cardiovascular diseases often lead to many years of physical limitations and burdens for patients and their families. Despite novel treatment methods, the body, for example, after a heart attack, cannot be fully restored to its previous functional capacity. However, with small steps, we can prevent the onset of disease early on!

Many factors influence the health of the heart and blood vessels. In addition to genetic and biological factors, lifestyle, stress experiences, physical and mental fitness, and daily behaviors play a crucial role in the development of cardiovascular diseases.

In the context of the study presented here, we aim to use well-established and innovative scientific methods to measure existing risk factors for the development of cardiovascular diseases early on in different individuals. We will also investigate how each person’s risk develops over the next 8 years. In the future, this improved description of individual risk will allow for timely, personalized therapies and interventions to be implemented for each person, preventing cardiovascular diseases from occurring.
conditions: Cardiovascular disease profiles and their known and exploratorily describable risk factors.

interventions.name: This is a single-arm, longitudinal, prospective observational study focusing on the occurrence of established and new risk factors for cardiovascular disease in subjects from the general population in Berlin and the surrounding area and in patients who have had cardiovascular disease for at least 6

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Informed consent capacity

Good proficiency in German, both spoken and written

Health insurance
Exclusion criteria:
Life expectancy (<6 months)

Refusal of blood sampling

Acute cardiac decompensation (<6 months)

Treatable psychiatric disorders (acute severe depressive episode)

Acute dialysis

Current chemotherapy / radiation (<6 months)

Pregnant & post-partum (mothers only after weaning)

Post-organ transplantation status (recipient)

Chronic and acute inflammatory bowel diseases
